seleniumProjectPath.description: Path to the existing Selenium Java + Cucumber project root, relative to the repo root. Use '.' when this system has been dropped directly into that repo.

targetProjectPath.description: Path to the Playwright TypeScript target project. Three supported states: (1) doesn't exist yet — the Engineer scaffolds it (see bootstrap.*); (2) an existing Playwright project (your own, or this system's bundled playwright-migrated/) — the Architect reads and adapts to its real structure before planning anything (see skills/target-project-discovery.skill.md); (3) the bundled playwright-migrated/ scaffold, which is just a pre-built instance of case 2.

migrationArtifactsPath.description: Path to the per-scenario requirements/plan/dev-log/test-report folders.

memory.description: Cross-session project memory — kept separate from the per-scenario migration/<slug>/ artifacts. See skills/project-memory.skill.md.

componentRegistryPath.description: Living index of every reusable step definition, page object, fixture, and hook that exists in targetProjectPath — kept current in real time so the Architect/Engineer can check for reuse without re-scanning the whole project.

changelogPath.description: Append-only chronological log, one entry per scenario the Validator signs off as passed.

bootstrap.description: Controls how the Engineer scaffolds targetProjectPath when it doesn't exist yet. See skills/target-project-bootstrap.skill.md.

autoCreateTargetProject.description: If true, the Engineer scaffolds a full playwright-bdd project at targetProjectPath (package.json, tsconfig.json, playwright.config.ts, folder structure) the first time it needs to implement into a path that has no package.json yet, then runs npm install / npx playwright install. If false, the Engineer stops and asks the user to scaffold it instead.

framework.description: Records the BDD architecture decision so every agent and skill assumes the same target shape without re-deciding it.

style.description: 'playwright-bdd' (default/recommended) compiles Gherkin .feature files + Cucumber-Expression step definitions into native Playwright tests. 'plain-playwright' generates test()/test.step() specs with no Gherkin layer instead — set automatically by skills/target-project-discovery.skill.md when targetProjectPath is an existing plain Playwright project and the user opts not to add playwright-bdd to it. See skills/plain-playwright-fallback.skill.md for what changes. Don't hand-edit this without also confirming targetProjectPath's real shape matches — it's an architecture fact, not a preference toggle.

sourceCucumberVersion.description: e.g. 'cucumber-jvm 7.x' — informs the Architect what Java-side step definition/DI conventions to expect.

seleniumSource.description: Where the Java-side Cucumber artifacts live, relative to seleniumProjectPath.

componentsDir.description: Shared composite UI components (header, nav, a modal) composed into page objects — see the Composite entry in design-patterns-and-solid.skill.md.

setupDir.description: Plain (non-BDD) Playwright test files for infrastructure setup, e.g. auth.setup.ts for storage-state authentication reuse.

testDir.description: Used only when framework.style is 'plain-playwright' — where generated *.spec.ts files live (featuresDir/stepsDir are unused in that mode).

stepDefinitionStyle.description: Prefer Cucumber Expressions ({string}, {int}, {word}) over regex — closer to what most Cucumber-JVM projects already use, more readable, less error-prone to write.

mode.description: The only supported mode: agents may only act on scenarios listed in `scenarios`. Hard guardrail, not a default to relax.

scenarios.description: The authoritative allow-list of Cucumber scenarios this system may touch. Only the Analyst adds entries here (when the user hands it a .feature file/scenario explicitly). Every other agent treats this list as read-only.

featureFile.description: Path to the .feature file, relative to seleniumSource.featuresDir.

scenario.description: Exact Scenario/Scenario Outline name from the .feature file, or "*" to mean every scenario currently in that file is in scope.
